newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish economy at risk of overheating - think tank.
newsitem.headline: Polish economy at risk of overheating - think tank.

text.p: Poland's economy risks overheating because of rising consumer credit, which should be contained by keeping interest rates unchanged, or increasing them, a private think-tank said on Thursday.
Bogdan Wyznikiewicz of the Gdansk Free Market Economy Research Institute (IBnGR) said household bank debts had increased 90 percent in 1996.
"This is something that must be tamed, because it is one of the factors behind the economic overheating," he told reporters.
IBnGR president Jan Szomburg expected the National Bank of Poland, the central bank, to increase interest rates.
"A rate rise is quite probable, because current circumstances discourage people from putting money in bank accounts," Szomburg said.
Szomburg said the Polish economy was prone to overheating because the capital market was not sufficiently developed and provided little alternative to consumer spending.

Institute analysts also pointed to rising real wages, which according to official forecasts, will increase 5.6 percent in 1996, as a factor that could contribute to overheating. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
